webthink_musique_iterative:
Solve a multi-hop question answering task by iteratively finding and reading relevance paragraphs.

You have access to a pool of 20 candidate paragraphs, but you must search to find the relevant ones.

Actions:
(1) Search[query]: Search for relevant paragraphs in the pool. Returns top 3 matches with snippets.
(2) Select[title]: Read the full content of a specific paragraph by its title.
(3) Finish[answer]: Submit the final answer.
(4) Lookup[keyword]: Find sentences containing a keyword in the currently selected paragraph.

Here are some examples.

Question: What year did the writer of 'Crazy Little Thing Called Love' die?
Thought 1: I need to find out who wrote 'Crazy Little Thing Called Love'. I will search for the song first.
Action 1: Search[Crazy Little Thing Called Love writer]
Observation 1: Title: Crazy Little Thing Called Love
Snippet: 'Crazy Little Thing Called Love' is a song by the British rock band Queen. Written by Freddie Mercury in 1979...

Title: Queen (band)
Snippet: Queen are a British rock band formed in London in 1970...

Thought 2: The snippet says it was written by Freddie Mercury. Now I need to find when Freddie Mercury died. I will search for him.
Action 2: Search[Freddie Mercury death year]
Observation 2: Title: Freddie Mercury
Snippet: Freddie Mercury (born Farrokh Bulsara; 5 September 1946 – 24 November 1991) was a British singer...

Thought 3: The snippet says he died on 24 November 1991. I should double check by reading the full paragraph to be sure.
Action 3: Select[Freddie Mercury]
Observation 3: Paragraph: Freddie Mercury
Content: Freddie Mercury (born Farrokh Bulsara; 5 September 1946 – 24 November 1991) was a British singer, songwriter, record producer, and lead vocalist of the rock band Queen. He is regarded as one of the greatest singers in the history of rock music. He died in 1991 from complications due to AIDS.

Thought 4: The text explicitly confirms he died in 1991. I can answer now.
Action 4: Finish[1991]
